concept: A single wall-facing sanding pad on a normal slide responds to a raised or recessed wall coupon. The same mechanism explains force control and local dwell; a wall elevation maps circular footprints around a real window opening.
model: Illustrative compliant contact: compression=max(0,4+bump-retreat) mm; F=5*compression N. Feedback moves retreat toward the force setpoint with 0.55 s response, 4 mm/s rate limit, ±4 mm travel. Above 45 N the example locks normal-axis advance. These are teaching settings, not tool recommendations.
coverage: Single 0.30 m disc; wall 3.6×2.4 m; window at (1.4,0.8), size 0.8×0.9 m. 0.08 m protection margin. Path segments contacting the expanded window or wall boundary are skipped with a lifted tool, never connected through the opening in contact. All parameter changes invalidate dry-run verification.
visual: Normal displacement uses 1.5 drawing units per mm. No spindle rotation is simulated; the time strip shows relative feed in dwell scenarios.
